summary: Hans T. Bakker is an Indologist who studied under Jacob Ensink (~1974–1982). He held a post at the University of Groningen (~1980–2013) and later served as a curator at the British Museum (2014).
Hans Windisch was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at Leiden University (1914–1929), Kiel University (~1929–1935), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1935).

Hans-Joachim Klimkeit was a scholar of religious, Iranian/Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and Gustav Mensching, whom he succeeded at the University of Bonn, serving as Direktor from 1972.
Hans-Werbin Köhler is an Indologist. He studied under Eduard Hermann and completed his doctoral work under Ernst Waldschmidt (attested 1973).
Hansa Dhammahaso is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. In 2017, he was attested as director at both the International Buddhist Studies College and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.
Hanung Kim is a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology. He earned a master's degree from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp.
Har Dayal was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1901–1903) and SOAS University of London (~1927–1932).

Hara Prasad Sastri was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (attested 1905) and Joint Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society (attested 1905–1911).

Harald Hauptmann was an archaeologist who completed his Promotion at Heidelberg University and Habilitation at the Free University of Berlin. He held a professorship at Heidelberg (1980–1994) and directed the German Archaeological Institute at Istanbul (1994–2001).

Haraprasad Shastri studied at Sanskrit College and University, Presidency University, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. His career included serving as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1900–1908) and department head at the University of Dhaka (1921–1924).

Hari Damodar Velankar was an Indologist who studied under Hari Mahadev Bhadkamkar. He held posts at Wilson College, Mumbai (attested 1944) and served as Joint Director of Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (attested 1959–1960).
Hari Shankar Prasad is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and completed studies under Ramakant Tripathi and Jan Willem de Jong.

Haridas Bhattacharyya was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned his master's degree at the University of Calcutta. He taught at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, the University of Dhaka, and Banaras Hindu University.
Haridas Sinharay is an Indologist who held a post at Central Calcutta College (attested 1970 and 1990).

Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate under Muni Jinvijaya. He taught at Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan (1945–1965), Gujarat University (1965–1975), and was later director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology.

Harjot Oberoi is a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the Australian National University before taking a chair at the University of British Columbia (~1987).
Harogadde Manappa Nayak was a scholar of linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1967–1991) and as Vice-chancellor of Gulbarga University (1984–1987).

Harold C. Conklin studied at UC Berkeley and Yale University. A scholar of linguistics and anthropology, he taught at Columbia University and held a professorship at Yale (1962–1996) alongside a curatorship at the Peabody Museum (1974–1996).

Harold Coward completed his doctorate in philosophy at McMaster University. He worked in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, serving as professor at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992) and director at the University of Victoria (~1992–2004).

Harold Hargreaves was a scholar in archaeology and Indology. He served as headmaster at Government Senior Secondary School, Amritsar (~1908–1914), and held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, including Deputy Director General (1928–1931).
